top_story.headline: Las Vegas consultant with German citizenship registers as foreign agent for Bavaria's economics ministry
top_story.dek: Margot Kiel's FARA registration statement was received by the Justice Department on Saturday.
paragraphs: Margot Kiel registered under the Foreign Agents Registration Act on October 24, 2026 (registration #7785). Her registration statement lists one foreign principal: the Bavarian State Ministry of Economic Affairs, Regional Development and Energy in Munich, Germany. The Justice Department's FARA unit stamped it received at 4:38 p.m. on October 24.

The filing gives her address as 11921 Amistoso Lane, Las Vegas, Nevada, lists her occupation as self-employed business consultant, and shows her citizenship as both United States and Germany. The OCR text available here does not show what she will do for the ministry or what she will be paid, and the DOJ bulk-file entry for her new registration lists no foreign principal yet.

Nothing else in today's input is bigger. The FARA search found no logged communications with the President, Vice President or a cabinet official. The one OGE item is a routine certification of ethics-agreement compliance.

sections.headline: Department of Labor Commissioner Certifies Ethics Agreement Compliance
paragraphs: Brett Matsumoto, the newly confirmed Commissioner of Labor Statistics, filed a Certification of Ethics Agreement Compliance certifying that he completed all required resignations and divestitures within the required timeframe.

items: Brett Matsumoto — Commissioner of Labor Statistics, Department of Labor. Certification of Ethics Agreement Compliance (signed October 2, 2026). Certified completion of all required resignations and all required divestitures indicated in his ethics agreement signed February 25, 2026, with divestitures confirmed via OGE Form 278-T filing on August 28, 2026. Certification.

blocks.text: Tracking 483 Senate-confirmed officials with ethics agreements since Jan. 20, 2025. Deadlines are counted from the confirmation date on congress.gov plus the agreement's stated window (usually 90 days) -- OGE can grant extensions that aren't public, so treat each flag as a lead to confirm, not a finding. OGE posts certifications with a lag, so nothing inside 30 days of a deadline is flagged. A certification filed but not yet posted by OGE will read as missing: confirm with the agency before publishing.
